translit: hṛiṣhīkeśhaṁ tadā vākyam idam āha mahī-pate
theme: Bow Raised, Heart Turns to Krishna
hindi: तब युद्ध शुरू होने ही वाला था। धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को युद्ध के लिए डटे हुए देखकर, हनुमानजी के ध्वज वाले पांडुपुत्र अर्जुन ने अपना धनुष उठाया और श्रीकृष्ण से ये वचन कहे, हे राजन्!
english: Then, as the clash of weapons was about to begin, Arjuna, the Pandava whose flag carried Hanuman, looked at Dhritarashtra’s sons standing in battle order. He lifted his bow and spoke these words to Krishna, O King.
deeper: This verse is like the quiet moment just before a big race. Both armies are in place, the conches have sounded, and the first arrows are about to fly. Arjuna has his bow in hand. He is ready, and he is brave. Sanjaya, who is telling the story, wants Dhritarashtra to see that moment clearly.

Notice two small details. Arjuna is called Kapi-dhwaja, “the one whose flag shows a monkey,” because Hanuman was on his chariot flag. A flag shows what a person stands for. Arjuna is also called Pandava, a son of Pandu. And he speaks to Hrishikesha, a name of Krishna meaning “master of the senses.” Arjuna turns to the one who is calm and steady, at a moment when his own mind is about to be shaken.

The verse is a doorway. Arjuna is about to say something very important, which we will hear in the next verses. For us the lesson is this: before the big moment, look honestly at what is in front of you, and turn to a wise guide. Being strong is good, and asking for guidance is even better.
words: the one whose flag bears a monkey (Hanuman), Arjuna
in the clash or release of weapons
to Hrishikesha, Krishna, master of the senses
O lord of the earth, O king (Dhritarashtra)
background: The great war of Kurukshetra was about to begin. Sanjaya was describing the battlefield to the blind King Dhritarashtra. The Kaurava side had blown its conches first, and then Krishna and Arjuna blew theirs (1.14–1.15). After that, the other Pandava warriors blew their own conches one by one (1.17–1.18).

The Pandava conches made such a thunder that the sky and earth rang and the hearts of Dhritarashtra’s sons shook (1.19). Now, in this verse, the armies stand in rows and the first weapons are about to be released. Arjuna lifts his bow and begins to speak to Krishna, who is his charioteer and friend.
lessons: Arjuna lifted his bow, yet he still paused to speak with Krishna before acting.
Arjuna looked carefully at the rows of people in front of him, and facing what is real is the first step to a wise choice.
Carry your ideals like a flag
Arjuna’s flag bore Hanuman, a sign of devotion, strength and courage.
At the big moment, Arjuna spoke to Krishna instead of acting alone.
Speak when your heart is full
Arjuna was about to share what he truly felt, and sharing with someone trustworthy helps us.
examples: Rohan’s team is standing on the field, and the first ball is about to be bowled. He takes a deep breath and looks at his captain for a last word of advice.
Meera sits with her pen ready and the question paper in front of her. Before writing, she reads the instructions slowly, because she wants to understand the paper before she starts.
Aarav is about to sing on stage at the school function. His knees feel wobbly, so he whispers to his teacher, “Will you stand where I can see you?”
Sana is about to ride her bicycle without side wheels for the first time. Her father stands beside her, and she looks at him before she pushes off.
Kabir’s school badge shows a lamp, which stands for knowledge. He remembers it when he is tempted to copy in a test, because it reminds him what his school stands for.
Telling the truth to a elder
Diya broke a flower pot and feels worried. She goes to her grandmother and says, “Ajji, I need to tell you something,” and she feels lighter right away.
Ishaan has to speak to a friend he fought with. Before running away, he stands still and looks at the whole situation to see what really happened.
Tara is nervous about a new school. Her older cousin Neha walks with her to the gate and says, “You can do this,” and Tara goes in with a steady heart.

story.title: Arjuna and the Eye of the Bird
paras: In the Mahabharata, the Kuru princes learned archery from their teacher Drona. One day he wanted to test them. He placed a wooden bird high up in a tree and asked each prince to take aim at it.
Before each prince shot, Drona asked, “What do you see?” One said, “I see the tree, the branches, the bird, and you, Gurudev.” Drona sent him away and said, “Lower your bow. You are not ready.”
When Arjuna’s turn came, Drona asked the same question. Arjuna answered, “I see only the eye of the bird.” Drona smiled and said, “Shoot.” The arrow struck the target exactly.

Years later, on the battlefield, Arjuna’s bow was raised again. This time the test was inside his heart. He was brave and trained, and he still turned to Krishna and spoke honestly. A good archer knows where to aim, and a wise person also knows whom to ask.
story.moral: Lesson: Be focused and ready for what is in front of you, and when the moment is big, turn to a wise guide.

quiz.q: Why is Arjuna called Kapi-dhwaja in this verse?
o: His flag showed Hanuman, the monkey
He had a monkey as a pet
quiz.x: Kapi-dhwaja means “one whose flag has a monkey,” because Hanuman was on Arjuna’s chariot flag.

quiz.q: What did Arjuna do when the weapons were about to clash?
o: He raised his bow and spoke to Krishna
quiz.x: He lifted his bow and then spoke to Hrishikesha, Krishna.

quiz.q: What does the name Hrishikesha mean?
quiz.x: Hrishikesha is a name of Krishna, meaning the master of the senses.

quiz.q: What is the main lesson of this verse for us?
o: Look honestly at the situation and turn to a wise guide
quiz.x: Arjuna looked at the situation clearly and turned to Krishna before the big moment.

reel.hook: Bow raised, battle begins… so why does Arjuna turn to Krishna?
reel.lesson: When the big moment comes, be ready, and turn to someone wise.
reel.caption:
Before every big moment, ask yourself who your Krishna is. 🏹
Today’s Gita verse: Arjuna lifts his bow and turns to his guide.
Who do you turn to when you feel nervous? 💛
